MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 21, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on January 21, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 16, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Leckness (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:10 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference With Legal Counsel--Anticipated Litigation. Based on Existing Facts and
  Circumstances, the City, Successor Agency and Housing Authority Will Confer with
  Legal Counsel and Provide Direction Regarding (i) Whether or Not to Initiate
  Litigation Pursuant to Section 54956.9(c)--One Potential Case.
City Council Minutes  1  January 21, 2013
 CS2. Labor Negotiations--The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are
  the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS3. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update on all three Closed
Session matters. The Council provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation to Former Mayor Ury

  Mayor Reardon presented a gavel plaque to Council Member Ury for his service as Mayor
  in 2012.

P2. Recognize the Fall AYSO Region 84, Boys U9 Silver Bullets for their Championship
  Season

  Mayor Reardon presented commendations to the coaches and members of the Silver Bullets
  team.

P3. Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners

  Michelle Clark, Waste Management, presented the senior single family resident recycling
  award to Sherman Rosenblum and Charlene Dubnow.

P4. Presentation by OCTA Regarding the Proposed I-5 Widening Project from SR-73 to
  El Toro Road

  The City Council received the presentation from Julie Toledo and Hamid Torkamanha of
  OCTA.

City Council Minutes  2  January 21, 2013
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: shared the sad news that Casta del Sol resident and former Community
Services Commissioner Gloria Heer passed away on January 13. A memorial service will be
held on February 2, 2013, at 2:00 p.m. at Fairhaven Memorial Services in Mission Viejo.

Amanda Bassett, Chair for the 2013 Relay for Life: thanked the City Council for supporting the
Relay for Life for the past 18 years and announced that during that time, the Relay has raised
over $2 million for the American Cancer Society. Mrs. Bassett announced that the annual kick-
off event will be held at the Murray Community Center on Thursday, January 24 at 6:00 p.m.
and she encouraged all to attend.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: introduced Nadadores Master Swimmer Allison Mitchell and
announced that the US National Masters Swim Championships will be held in Mission Viejo
from August 7 through 11, 2013. The Nadadores are looking for sponsorships from Mission
Viejo businesses and more information can be found at www.mastersmvnswim.org. Mrs.
Bucknum also expressed her support for item 16, the annexation of land for the Skyridge
development.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: stated that a real example of perseverance is the man who we honor today, Dr.
Martin Luther King, Jr. Mr. Hayes presented the Council Members with a packet of information
on Dr. King and highlighted excerpts from the I Have a Dream speech.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 11, 13, 14 and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

4.  Check Register dated December 21, 2012 in the amount of $7,103,795.13

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  3  January 21, 2013
 5.  Check Register dated January 4, 2013 in the amount of $637,342.48

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2012

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for November 2012

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2012

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2012

  Received and filed.

10. Mileage Reimbursement

  Adopted Resolution 13-03 Adopting the Standard IRS Mileage Reimbursement Rate of
  56.5 Cents Per Mile for the Period From January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2013.

12. General Plan Progress Report for 2012

  Received and filed report.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council/Agency Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht requested that her comments be modified on page 11 of the
  January 7, 2013, Minutes to reflect that Smart Meters and the opt-out fee violate a person's
  constitutional rights.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to (1) approve
  the Minutes for the special meeting of December 21, 2012, as presented; and (2) approve
  the Minutes for the regular meeting of January 7, 2013, as amended.

City Council Minutes  4  January 21, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Ury

  (Pursuant to City Council Policy, an abstention will be viewed as support for the majority
  decision.)

3.  Check Register dated December 14, 2012 in the amount of $2,102,912.23

  Council Member Schlicht asked for an explanation of the fee paid to Psomas for
  professional services related to the Ferrocarril slope.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon responded that the consultant is assisting staff
  with evaluation of the project and the possible implementation of an assessment district.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13. Funding for Purchase of Two Replacement Public Services Fleet Vehicles

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay explained staff's
  recommendation to replace two Public Services trucks due to the age and mileage on the
  vehicles and the need for fuel cell replacements.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to adopt Resolution
  13-06 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget for Costs Related to the Replacement
  of Two Public Services Fleet Vehicles.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. Grant Application to the California State Parks and Recreation Department for a
  Pedestrian Ramp Along the Oso Creek Trail and the Adjacent Commercial Core

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commended staff for recognizing the opportunity for this grant and
City Council Minutes  5  January 21, 2013
   stated that a pedestrian ramp will be a great enhancement to the Oso Creek Trail.
  Council Member Schlicht stated that she will be voting against this item because it appears
  to her that it is another make-work project for the vendors. She feels that more people need
  to say no to the ways in which the Council is asked to spend money.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to adopt Resolution
  13-07 Approving a Potential Contract Agreement with the State of California Department
  of Parks and Recreation for a Pedestrian Ramp from the Oso Creek Trail to the Adjacent
  Commercial Core and Designating the City Manager as the Agent to Administer and Sign
  the Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

15. Senior Citizen Transportation Contract Agreements with Orange County Transportation
  Authority (OCTA), Age Well Senior Services, Inc. and California Yellow Cab

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley noted that staff has been successful in proposing a contract with
  OCTA that will almost double the current senior Dial-A-Taxi transportation services,
  saving the city about $40,000 annually. She announced that Mission Viejo seniors will
  receive $120,000 in transportation services with a cost of only $13,000 to the City.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  approve entering into a Contract Agreement with the Orange County Transportation
  Authority (OCTA) (A13-01) to receive grant funds for Senior Citizen Transportation
  Services in the amount of approximately $50,000 through June 30, 2013, and
  approximately $100,000 annually through June 30, 2016; (2) approve entering into a
  Contract Agreement with Age Well Senior Services, Inc. (A13-02) to provide
  transportation services for the Senior Citizen Nutrition program in the amount of $17,500
  through June 30, 2013, and $35,000 annually through June 30, 2016; (3) and approve
  Amendment No. 6 to the Contract with California Yellow Cab to provide Senior Citizen
  Dial-A-Taxi Transportation Services in the amount of $39,000 through June 30, 2013, and
  $78,000 annually through June 30, 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Ury

  (Pursuant to City Council Policy, an abstention will be viewed as support for the majority decision.)
City Council Minutes  6  January 21, 2013
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

16. General Plan Amendment GPA2012-30, Zone Change ZC2012-19, Vesting Tentative
  Tract Map VTTM 17392, Planned Development Permit PDP2012-247, and Temporary
  Use Permit TUP2012-288, being petitions submitted by Peter Carlson of Vandermost
  and Carlson, agent for Standard Pacific Corporation, for the Northeast Annexation
  Area and Skyridge project. The project involves the annexation of approximately 40-
  acres into the City of Mission Viejo by the Local Agency Formation Commission
  (LAFCO). General Plan Amendment GPA2012-30 and Zone Change ZC2012-19 are
  filed to establish land use designations and pre-annexation zoning. Vesting Tentative
  Tract Map 17392, Planned Development Permit PDP2012-247, and Temporary Use
  Permit TUP2012-288 are filed by Standard Pacific Corporation for the construction of
  84 single-family detached residential dwelling units on approximately 28.5 acres of the
  larger 40-acre site. The project site is located along the east side of El Toro Road north
  of the SR-241 Toll Road in the County of Orange, California. The project site is located
  south of the intersection of Live Oak Canyon Road and El Toro Road/Santiago Canyon
  Road; Glenn Ranch Road and Ridgeline Drive are located south and north of the site,
  respectively. The properties included in the Sphere of Influence are as follows: APN
  Nos. 856-061-06, 856-061-15, 856-061-17, 856-061-31, 856-061-33, 856-061-21, 856-061-
  30, 856-061-40, and 856-061-41. Also under consideration is the authorization for the
  City of Mission Viejo to make application to LAFCO for the proposed annexation area,
  a proposed Property Tax Exchange Agreement between the City of Mission Viejo and
  the County of Orange, and a Pre-Annexation Agreement between the City of Mission
  Viejo and the County of Orange.

  Community Development Director Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Planning Manger Elaine Lister provided background and an overview of the proposed
  project.

  Mayor Reardon opened the public hearing at 7:38 p.m.

  Michael Battaglia, Vice President of Project Development for Standard Pacific
  Corporation: presented an outline of the proposed Skyridge project and the reasons that
  they wish to have the property annexed to Mission Viejo.

  Peter Carlson, Environmental Consultant, Vandermost and Carlson: summarized the
  Environmental Impact Report (EIR) and the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  review process.

  The following expressed support for the proposed annexation: Warren Inouye, M.V.; Jon
  Robertson, M.V.; Kevin Lange, M.V.; John Wilkins, M.V.; Patrick Parker, M.V.; Frank
  Sanchez, Trabuco Canyon; Robert David Breton, M.V.; and Scott Starkey, M.V.

City Council Minutes  7  January 21, 2013
   The following presented comments in opposition to the proposed annexation: Joyce
  Stonfield Pery, Irvine (asked for provisions to document and educate the community on the
  Indians that were indigenous to that area); Dan Fischman, Trabuco Canyon; and Kathleen
  Stockwell, M.V.

  The following presented written comments (via email) expressing support for the proposed
  annexation: William Wilhelm, M.V. and Gigi Becker.

  The following presented written comments (via email) expressing opposition to the
  proposed annexation: Harry Lenczyk, M.V. and Donna Dahl, M.V.

  Mr. Carlson responded to resident comments and stated that they will gladly provide a
  monument to identify the Native American history of the area. He also outlined the traffic
  analysis included in the EIR and concerns with coastal sage scrub and the gnatcatcher bird.

  Mr. Battaglia announced that they will work with the post office to have the zip code
  changed to a Mission Viejo zip code. He also discussed HOA budgets for maintenance of
  common property.

  At the hour of 8:54 p.m., Mayor Reardon closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 13-08 Certifying the Final Environmental Impact Report; (2) adopt Resolution
  13-09 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2012-30 for the 40-Acre Sphere of
  Influence and Annexation Area; (3) introduce Ordinance 13-295 entitled An Ordinance of
  the City of Mission Viejo, California, Adopting Chapter 9.16 - Estate Residential Overlay
  Zone of Title 9 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code and Pre-Zoning, to Become the
  Permanent Zoning of a 40-Acre Parcel in the County of Orange, California (Zone Change
  ZC2012-19); (4) adopt Resolution 13-10 Approving Vesting Tentative Tract Map
  VTTM17392, Planned Development Permit PDP2012-247, and Temporary Use Permit
  TUP2012-288 for the Construction of 84 Single-Family Detached Residential Dwelling
  Units on Approximately 28.5 Acres of the Larger 40-Acre Site; (5) adopt Resolution 13-11
  Making Application to and Requesting the Local Agency Formation Commission of
  Orange County to Take Proceedings Pursuant to the Cortese-Knox-Hertzberg Local
  Government Reorganization Act of 2000 for the City of Mission Viejo to Annex the 40-
  Acre Sphere of Influence and Annexation area; (6) adopt Resolution 13-12 Approving a
  Property Tax Exchange Agreement between the City of Mission Viejo and the County of
  Orange (A13-04) for the 40-Acre Sphere of Influence and Annexation Area; and (7)
  approve Pre-Annexation Agreement between the City of Mission Viejo and the County of
  Orange (A13-03) for the 40-acre Sphere of Influence and Annexation area.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  January 21, 2013
 RECESS

At the hour of 9:06 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
9:22 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

OLD BUSINESS

17. Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Steven Miles, Miles Law Group, Attorney for Sunset Property Services: expressed concern
  with Athens' use of the City's contracted rate or "tipping fee" at the County dump and stated
  that Sunset Property Services and the other bidders were not aware of this discount when
  providing a bid for the street sweeping contract.

  Gary Clifford, Chief Operating Officer, Athens Services: stated that Athens was aware of
  the dumping fee when providing a bid and accounted for that in their price. He noted that
  Athens asked for the City's landfill rate at the appropriate time, after winning the bid.

  John Howhannesian, Sunset Property Services: responded to questions about Sunset's
  choice to absorb the cost for not using the City's tipping fee at the dump. He stated that
  Sunset was the lowest responsible bidder for 17 years and followed all of the provisions
  that were outlined in their contract.

  The following presented a written comment (via email) in favor of maintaining the current
  contract with Athens: Art Cook, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury to (1) approve First Amendment to the existing
  contract with Arakelian Enterprises, Inc., dba Athens Services for the period of July 1,
  2013, through June 30, 2015, in an amount not to exceed $673,868.00; and (2) authorize
  staff to issue a purchase order to Arakelian Enterprises, Inc., dba Athens Services in an
  amount not to exceed $336,934.00. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to reject
  staff's recommendation and direct staff to rebid the street sweeping contract.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  9  January 21, 2013
 18. Update on Adopted Ordinance Relating to Commercial Real Estate Signs

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson announced that staff has had success
  in enforcing the new sign standards and, in general, Mission Viejo is more in line with the
  needs of the real estate community in this type of economy.

  The following presented written comments (via email) expressing opposition to the
  increased size of real estate signs: Art Cook, M.V.; Harry Lenczyk, M.V.; Donna Dahl,
  M.V.; and Frank and Betty Gilliland.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  receive and file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to direct staff to
  return with an agenda item regarding rescission of the ordinance that increased the size of
  commercial real estate signage.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

19. Commercial Signage - Review of Prohibited Signs Request for Direction Regarding
  Revising, in Full or Part, Mission Viejo Municipal Code Section 9.29.230 or the
  Direction to Not Prepare Revisions to this Section.

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and reminded the Council that they will
  not be deciding on the Kaleidoscope signage proposal this evening. Instead the Council is
  asked to address the overall commercial signage code and determine if the code is still
  current or needs updating.

  Robert David Breton, M.V.: speaking as a former Council Member with knowledge of the
  City's original sign ordinance, he stated that a change to the sign code will alter the goals
  and objectives of the community and will change the very fabric of Mission Viejo. Mr.
  Breton noted that a proposal to allow digital electronic signage threatens to open the flood
  gates to the kind of signage that plagues other cities and he urged the Council to remain
  true to the City's founding documents.

City Council Minutes  10  January 21, 2013
   Colby Durnin, Kaleidoscope: presented an overview of the Kaleidoscope signage proposal.

  At the hour of 12:00 a.m., Mayor Reardon vacated the dais. Mayor Reardon returned to the
  dais at 12:02 a.m.

  The following spoke in support of commercial sign code revisions and the Kaleidoscope
  signage proposal: Dan Lauriano, M.V.; Jim Leach, Chairman of the South Orange County
  Regional Chamber of Commerce Economic Coalition; Donna Varner, Chair of the South
  Orange County Regional Chambers of Commerce, M.V.; Mike Conte, M.V.; and Colby
  Durnin, Kaleidoscope, M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to sign code revisions: JudyBullockus, M.V.; Robert
  David Breton, M.V.; Helen Workun, M.V.; and Steve Magdziak, M.V.

  The following presented written comments (some via email) in opposition to modifying the
  City's sign code and large or electronic billboards: John Reed, M.V.; MaryEllen Lewis,
  M.V.; Herb Abrams, M.V.; Donna Dahl, M.V.; Don Wilder, M.V.; Art Cook, M.V.; Harry
  Lenczyk, M.V.; Hugh and Karen Lander, M.V.; Larry Gilbert, M.V.; Pat Herr, M.V.; Frank
  and Betty Gilliland, M.V.; Barbara Kogerman, Mayor of the City of Laguna Hills;
  Elizabeth Busick, M.V.; Howard Esterman, M.V.; and Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V  .

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to make no
  amendments to the City's sign code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

11. Modifying the Employee Contribution Towards PERS Member Contributions and
  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule

  Council Member Schlicht asked that the recommended action be bifurcated into two

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-04 Modifying the Employer Paid Member Contributions to the California

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  11  January 21, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-05 Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary Ranges for
  Authorized Job Classifications.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

  Council Member Ury nominated Steven Spillman to serve on the Planning and
  Transportation Commission, Brian Porter to serve on the Community Services Commission

  Council Member Schlicht nominated Ellen Addonizio to serve on the Investment Advisory
  Commission.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to approve

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.
City Council Minutes  12  January 21, 2013
 24. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

25. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

26. City Council FY 2013-2015 Pre-Budget Discussion

  City Manager Wilberg asked the Council Members to read the report and be prepared to
  discuss it at the next meeting. The Council will be asked to review the strategic goals and
  concur that those are still valid. He also asked the Council to consider staff's
  recommendation to provide funds for existing service levels and use any additional

City Attorney’s Report

27. Ordinance Establishing an Employee Disclosure Program for Local Enactments and

  Section 2.80

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

  Gas & Electric ("SDGE") Joint Application for Increased Funding for the Trust
  Fund Intended to Pay for the Decommissioning of San Onofre’s Nuclear Generator
  Units 2 and 3

  Continued to the next City Council Meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

29. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

City Council Minutes  13  January 21, 2013
 Council Member Leckness

Due to the late hour, Council Member Leckness postponed his comments until the next meeting.

Council Member Schlicht

30. Annual Routine Landscape Contracts

  Council Member Schlicht continued this item to the next City Council Meeting.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury postponed his comments until the next meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she will place an item on the next agenda to consider
planning an event for the community's 50th anniversary and the City's 25th anniversary.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that the Elks Club will hold its annual dinner to honor police and fire
personnel on Saturday, January 26, 2013. She noted that she will close the meeting in honor of
former Community Services Commissioner Gloria Heer who was a tireless supporter of parks
and recreation. Mrs. Heer was highly recognized by national and state organizations and in
1982, the Los Angeles Board of Supervisors named a park after Gloria as a thank you for her
contributions and years of service on the LA Parks and Recreation Committee. Mayor Reardon
announced that a memorial service will be held for Mrs. Heer on February 2, 2013, at 2:00 p.m.
at Fairhaven Memorial in Mission Viejo.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 1:34 a.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Gloria Heer to Monday, February 4, 2013,
at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 4, 2013

City Council Minutes  14  January 21, 2013
